A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same research work. Their methods, equations, experiments, figures and tables can be matched reliably. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A–C.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report original feature visualizations, synthetic function approximation and UCI regression results in Figure 1 and Tables 1–3, alongside baseline results attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds numerical baseline comparisons, feature-count experiments and ablations, including original results in Tables 4–6.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains the linear output-weight solve, learned feature distribution, latent-space Adam refinement and total-variation regularization. GFT-p is renamed GFT-r. F-Opt's direct reduced-loss optimization was already described in v1; the new experimental controls do not revise the proposed GFT procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate g1–g3, f1–f3, h1–h3 and the same six UCI datasets: Propulsion, Galaxy, Airfoil, CCPP, Telemonit and Skillkraft. The new appendices vary feature counts and training procedures on existing tasks, without adding data domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds F-Opt and Gaussian kernel ridge regression to each of Tables 1–3. Figure 1 additionally evaluates conventional neural-network training, previously absent from that comparison. Appendix B introduces fully sampled weights and noisy-gradient controls, substantially expanding the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: New settings include N=50 and N=200 in Appendix A, joint feature/output-weight sampling and noisy SGD with noise strength 0.1 times the step size in Appendix B, and a median-rule Gaussian kernel. Existing experiments retain their splits, metrics, regularization search and stated GFT training budget; Appendix C's disclosures do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's refinement comparisons and feature visualization, v2 tests direct feature optimization, sensitivity to feature count, replacing the analytic output-weight solve with joint sampling, and adding gradient noise. Appendices A–B and the expanded Figure 1 provide substantial new evidence about component necessity and optimization behavior.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run mean test MSEs. Tables 4–6 extend the same reporting practice, without adding seed information, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests or an increased repeat count.

E6.justification: Matched scores in Tables 1–3 and retained Figure 1 panels are unchanged. v2 adds F-Opt, kernel-ridge and neural-network visualization results, plus extensive width and ablation results in Tables 4–6. These also expose sensitivity: Table 5 reports Fourier GFT-r MSE 1.82 for f3 with d=10, M=200 and N=200, an added setting rather than a revised original score.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 newly states that the regularized solution of equation (6) converges to the minimum-norm solution of equation (5) as epsilon approaches zero. This adds a limited mathematical property; the core derivations remain unchanged and no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph and discussion retain the same central claims: learned feature proposals, analytically solved output weights, latent refinement and regularization improve training of thin two-layer networks on small datasets. The additional evidence does not redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the categorical minibatching prohibition with a discussion of batch-dependent output weights and explicitly states the squared-loss restriction. Appendix B explains why jointly sampled output weights underperform. Section 4.2 qualifies support recovery by acknowledging off-support features, while Remark 1 discusses extension to vector-valued outputs.

D1.justification: Appendix C supplies settings that v1 left to the code: learning rates of 1e-4 for GFT/refinement and 1e-3 for neural networks, 100000 neural-network steps, epsilon=1e-7 and 1000 regularization samples. These are newly documented details; the code address, GPU and reported runtime remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds connections to extreme learning machines, Dunbar et al.'s adaptive random-feature work and implicit kernel learning, while sharpening distinctions from sparse feature selection and alternating updates. Kernel-regression and UCI references are also added. Publication updates for existing references do not represent new related works.

P1.justification: v2 edits prose, replaces GFT-p/post-processing terminology with GFT-r/feature refinement, converts Example 1 into bullets and expands the explanation of compared methods. It adds Appendices A–C and updates author/publication information, while retaining the main section sequence and narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands from nine to twelve panels through a new neural-network row. Tables 1–3 gain comparator rows and are reflowed, while three new tables present appendix experiments. Best-score highlighting gains boldface, and publication headers are added.

improvement.justification: The F-Opt comparisons and Appendix B controls address an important gap in v1 by directly testing the roles of learned proposals and analytically solved output weights. Width experiments and explicit implementation settings further strengthen empirical scrutiny and reproducibility. These are substantial gains, although five-run means still lack dispersion estimates and the newly exposed width-dependent failures receive little interpretation.
